Looking at this problem, I need to analyze the relationship between continuous homomorphisms from a pro-$p$ group $G$ into $\mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$ and into $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$.

## Proof

**Setup and key identifications.**

The group $\mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$ is the Prüfer $p$-group $C_{p^\infty}$, equipped with the discrete topology (since $\mathbb{Z}_p$ is open in $\mathbb{Q}_p$, the quotient is discrete). It is canonically isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]/\mathbb{Z}$, which is precisely the $p$-primary torsion subgroup of $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$.

The group $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$ decomposes as a direct sum of its primary components:
$$\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z} \;=\; \bigoplus_{\ell \text{ prime}} \mathbb{Q}_\ell/\mathbb{Z}_\ell \;=\; (\mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p) \;\oplus\; \left(\bigoplus_{\ell \neq p} \mathbb{Q}_\ell/\mathbb{Z}_\ell\right).$$

Under this decomposition, there is a canonical inclusion $i: \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p \hookrightarrow \mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$.

**The induced map.**

The inclusion $i$ induces a map by post-composition:
$$i_*: \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,\, \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p) \;\longrightarrow\; \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,\, \mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}).$$

We claim $i_*$ is a bijection.

**Injectivity.** If $i \circ \varphi = i \circ \psi$ for continuous homomorphisms $\varphi, \psi: G \to \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$, then since $i$ is injective, $\varphi = \psi$.

**Surjectivity — the key step.**

Let $\varphi: G \to \mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$ be a continuous homomorphism. We show $\varphi$ factors through $i$.

*Step 1: The image $\varphi(G)$ is finite.*

The group $G$ is pro-$p$, hence compact. The group $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$ is Hausdorff (whether given the discrete topology, or the subspace topology inherited from $S^1 = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$). A continuous image of a compact space in a Hausdorff space is compact, hence closed. So $\varphi(G)$ is a compact subgroup of $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$.

- If $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$ is discrete, compactness forces $\varphi(G)$ to be finite.
- If $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$ carries the subspace topology from $S^1$, then any infinite subgroup of $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$ is dense in $S^1$ (or in some closed arc), hence not closed in $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$, hence not compact. So again $\varphi(G)$ is finite.

In either case, $\varphi(G)$ is a **finite** subgroup of $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$.

*Step 2: The image $\varphi(G)$ is a $p$-group.*

Since $\varphi$ is a homomorphism, $\varphi(G) \cong G / \ker(\varphi)$ is a finite quotient of $G$. Because $G$ is pro-$p$, every finite quotient of $G$ is a finite $p$-group. Therefore $\varphi(G)$ is a finite $p$-group.

*Step 3: The image lands in the $p$-primary component.*

A finite $p$-group has no elements of order $\ell$ for any prime $\ell \neq p$. Under the decomposition $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z} = \bigoplus_\ell (\mathbb{Q}_\ell/\mathbb{Z}_\ell)$, the projection of $\varphi(G)$ onto each $\ell$-primary component ($\ell \neq p$) is a $p$-group that is also an $\ell$-group, hence trivial. Therefore:
$$\varphi(G) \;\subseteq\; \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p.$$

*Step 4: Factorization.*

Since $\varphi(G) \subseteq \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$, the map $\varphi$ factors uniquely through $i$: there exists a unique homomorphism $\widetilde{\varphi}: G \to \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$ with $i \circ \widetilde{\varphi} = \varphi$. Both $\mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$ and $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$ are discrete, so $\widetilde{\varphi}$ is continuous (the preimage of any point is the same as under $\varphi$, which is open since $\varphi$ is continuous and the target is discrete). Thus $\widetilde{\varphi} \in \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(G, \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p)$ and $i_*(\widetilde{\varphi}) = \varphi$.

This proves surjectivity.

**Naturality.**

The bijection $i_*$ is natural in $G$: for any continuous homomorphism $f: G' \to G$ of pro-$p$ groups, the diagram
$$\require{AMScd}
\begin{CD}
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(G, \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p) @>{i_*}>> \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(G, \mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z})\\
@V{f^*}VV @V{f^*}VV\\
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(G', \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p) @>{i_*}>> \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(G', \mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z})
\end{CD}$$
commutes, since both paths are simply $\varphi \mapsto i \circ \varphi \circ f$. The bijection is induced by the canonical inclusion of the $p$-Prüfer group as the $p$-primary torsion of $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$, requiring no choices.

**Conclusion.**

There is a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,\, \mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p) \;\cong\; \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,\, \mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}),$$
given by the canonical inclusion $\mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p \hookrightarrow \mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$. The essential reason is that every continuous homomorphism from a pro-$p$ group $G$ into $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$ has finite $p$-group image, which necessarily lands in the $p$-primary component $\mathbb{Q}_p/\mathbb{Z}_p$.
